root_cause.text: The function blkcg_maybe_throttle_current() fails to release a disk reference obtained via get_device() on error paths (blkcg lookup, blkg lookup, or blkg_tryget failure), because the “out” label only calls rcu_read_unlock() and does not include put_disk(), causing a disk reference leak.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds put_disk(disk) to the “out” label. The commit message states: “Add the missing put_disk() on the error path … When blkcg lookup, blkg lookup, or blkg_tryget() fails, the function jumps to the out label which only calls rcu_read_unlock() but does not release the disk reference acquired by blkcg_schedule_throttle() via get_device().” It also notes that current->throttle_disk is already set to NULL, so blkcg_exit() cannot release the reference.

intent_record.what: Added a call to put_disk(disk) in the out: error label of blkcg_maybe_throttle_current to release the disk reference before returning.
intent_record.how: Before the change, the error path leaked a disk reference because get_disk was called but not matched with put_disk. After the change, put_disk decrements the reference count, preventing resource leak.
